Strategic_Context: [Customer Company Name], a leading company, is focused on strengthening its data ecosystem to enable faster, data-driven decision-making across its enterprise operations.
To support modernization and future scalability, [Customer Name] plans to migrate its enterprise data warehouse from Snowflake (legacy environment) to the Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
Onix, in partnership with Google, will deliver a structured, low-risk migration program that leverages its proven methodology and deep experience in modernizing data platforms.
The assessment will specifically identify technical debt and optimization opportunities to ensure the target GCP environment maximizes ROI and minimizes operational overhead.
Business_Drivers: Defined Business Drivers: Explicitly list the Customer's primary business objectives driving the assessment (e.g., exiting an on-prem data center by a specific date, reducing licensing costs, or optimizing specific query performance) to tie the technical assessment to a tangible ROI.

Eagle_Methodology: Eagle is Onix's proprietary workshop accelerator used to analyze and migration for existing data warehouse environments and support cloud migration planning.

Eagle extracts and analyzes metadata, SQL scripts, ETL workflows, orchestration jobs, and Bl dependencies to provide insights into data assets, lineage, usage patterns, and code complexity without accessing business data.
For [Customer Name], Onix will utilize Eagle to assess the existing Snowflake, DataStage, Databricks, and Power Bl environments.
Eagle will generate detailed object inventory, end-to-end lineage, and volumetric analysis to support migration planning and migrations work.

Based on this workshop, Onix will deliver the future-state architecture on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), migration approach, effort estimates, and a detailed migration Statement of Work (SOW), ensuring a scalable, efficient, and low-risk modernization of [Customer Name] data platform.
Assessment_Execution_Approach: Tooling Methodology: Datametica Eagle uses a non-intrusive, read-only connection to source system metadata repositories and query logs, ensuring zero impact on production system performance during the assessment.
Onix proposes a Solution Approach in the following phases: 1. Discovery and Analysis, 2. Design and Recommendations

Discovery_and_Analysis_Activities: To fulfill the service objectives of this engagement, Onix will perform the following activities:

1. Discovery & Analysis: a. Snowflake metadata analysis: object counts, table sizes, active/inactive analysis; b. Data lineage and object access analysis (stored procedures, views, SQL scripts, user access patterns); c. DataStage analysis: volumetrics, complexity, job-level lineage; d. Orchestration inventory and lineage (Control-Mexport analysis); e. Power Bl metadata and volumetrics analysis; f. Databricks metadata analysis (Unity Catalog export), jobs/workflows lineage, notebooks review; g. Consolidation of lineage, object classification, and move groups.

2. Design and Recommendations: a. High-level future-state technical and solution architecture; b. High-level migration project plan; c. Migration SOW and estimates; d. Final readout and assessment report.
Comprehensive_Assessments: Automated Code Complexity Scoring: Include a detailed breakdown of SQL/ETL script complexity (Simple, Medium, Complex) generated by the Datametica Eagle tool to accurately forecast automated translation vs. manual refactoring efforts.
Target GCP Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Estimation: Expand the design recommendations to include forecasted GCP consumption costs (e.g., BigQuery compute/storage) based on current workload volumes.
Security and Compliance Architecture Mapping: Include an assessment of current data security policies (RBAC, masking, encryption) and map them to native GCP security controls.
Deliverables_Milestone_1: 1. Snowflake Metadata Analysis: a. Count of Tables, views, indexes, and triggers; b. Size of tables
2. Data Lineage and Object Access Analysis: a. Active/Inactive; b. User access analysis and Table access patterns
3. DataStage: a. Volumetrics and complexity Analysis
6. Databricks Metadata Analysis: a. Count of Tables, views, indexes, triggers; b. Size of tables
8. High-Level Project Plan, Future State Architecture, Migration SOW
Deliverables_Milestone_2_Data_Migrations: 1. Data Lineage and Object Access Analysis: a. Stored procedures to tables; b. Views to tables; c. SQL scripts lineage
2. DataStage: a. Sequence and parallel jobs level lineage; b. Parallel to the source and target table
4. Other Object analysis: a. Notebooks analysis; b. Volumetrics
Migration_Planning_Deliverables: Eagle Translation Feasibility Report: A definitive deliverable identifying the percentage of legacy code (Snowflake SQL, DataStage ETL) that Datametica tools can auto-translate versus code requiring manual rewrites.
Workload Migration Wave Plan: A prioritized backlog of 'Move Groups' structured into executable phases based on the extracted dependency and lineage data.

Execution_and_System_Limitations: Activities not enumerated in Section 2.1, which also extends to include the following:
(a) Any development, migration execution, or production cutover activities and foundation finish out
(b) Assessment of platforms/tools not explicitly listed in scope
(c) System upgrades, patching, or third-party licensing
(e) Assessment limited to provided production metadata/logs and code extracts only
(f) POC limited to MVPs and benchmarks
Performance Tuning of Legacy Systems: Any optimization or tuning of the existing Snowflake, DataStage, or Databricks environments during the assessment period.
Tooling_and_Volumetric_Caps: Volumetric Caps (Scope Creep Protection): Assessment is limited to a specified maximum number of tables, ETL jobs, and Terabytes of log data. Anything beyond the cap requires a Change Request.

Tooling Limitations: Datametica Eagle's automated parsing covers standard SQL/ETL components; heavily obfuscated or encrypted legacy code may require manual review, limited to a specific number of hours.
Data_Handling_and_Security_Exclusions: Data Quality and Data Cleansing: Explicitly state that assessing the quality of existing business data, identifying duplicate records, or resolving data integrity issues prior to migration is out of scope.

PII/PHI Identification within Payloads: While metadata is analyzed, scanning or identifying Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or Protected Health Information (PHI) within actual data payloads is out of scope.

Duration_and_Phasing: Phase 1 (Weeks 1 & 2): Eagle Setup, Eagle Prerequisites Gathering, Snowflake Metadata and Log processing, Datastage Volumentrics, Databricks/Power BI Analysis, High level Future state architecture, High level Project Plan and Complete Migration SOW.
Phase 2 (Weeks 3 to 7): Snowflake Database and external scripts Lineage, Datastage Lineage, Consolidation of Lineage, Object classification and Move Groups, Final Readout of Eagle deliverables.
Governance_Tollgates: Phase Tollgates: Require formal stakeholder sign-off at the end of Milestone 1 before project resources fully commence Milestone 2 activities to ensure alignment on initial findings.

Primary_Delivery_Criteria: 1. Complete metadata, lineage, and volumetrics workshop across in-scope systems
2. High-level future-state architecture and migration strategy
3. Migration SOW and project plan aligned to business priorities
4. Low-risk execution approach with clear prerequisites and governance
Quality_and_Accuracy_Criteria: Eagle Log Processing Completeness: Successfully ingesting and processing a mutually agreed-upon historical window (e.g., 30 to 90 days) of query logs to ensure statistically significant usage pattern analysis.
Actionable Migration SOW: The resulting migration SOW must contain a +/- 15% confidence interval on effort and timeline estimation derived from the Datametica Eagle complexity scoring.
Alignment_Criteria: Stakeholder Alignment: Formal sign-off on the future-state architecture and migration wave plan by the Customer's enterprise architecture board or executive sponsors.
